words.gloss: breaking pain of teeth and bones
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

words.gloss: defects of hair, body-hair, nails and beard
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: अध्यस्थि और अधिदन्त, दाँतों और अस्थियों में भेदन-शूल, विवर्णता, तथा केश, लोम, नख और श्मश्रु के दोष अस्थि के प्रदोष से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: Adhyasthi and adhidanta (extra bone and extra tooth), breaking pain of the teeth and bones, discolouration, and defects of the hair, body-hair, nails and beard arise from vitiation of bone (asthi).

text_flags.why: possible: medas in a compound takes the form medo-/medaḥ-, not meda-, so 'meda-śūla' is not a regular compound of medas; bheda 'breaking' fits a list of bone disorders (cf. bheda- in 22 of this chunk, bhedaśoṣapradūṣaṇam); the syllable count (16) is the same

notes: adhyasthidantau is read as a dual dvandva 'adhyasthi and (adhi)danta', the prefix adhi- understood with danta from adhyasthi; the names are kept in Sanskrit with a literal gloss. The words are split from the conjectured dantāsthibhedaśūlaṃ (see text_flag); printed -meda- cannot be a regular compound form of medas. bheda-śūla may also be a dvandva 'breaking and pain'. doṣa here = defects, not the bodily doṣas. Continues the list of disorders by dhātu begun before this chunk (vidyān māṃsāśrayān ... medaḥsaṃśrayān ...).

hindi: पर्वों में पीड़ा, भ्रम, मूर्च्छा तथा अन्धकार का दिखाई देना, और पर्वों में उत्पन्न मोटी जड़ वाले अरुषों का दिखाई देना —
english: Pain in the small joints (parvan), giddiness, mūrcchā and the seeing of darkness, and the appearance of aruṣ (sores) with thick roots arising at the joints —
notes: SENTENCE: the list continues into 18, where majjapradoṣāt 'from vitiation of marrow' gives its cause. darśanam is used twice: 'seeing' of darkness (by the patient) and 'appearance' of the sores. aruṣ is kept in Sanskrit with the literal gloss 'sores'; the case is gen. pl. of the stem aruṣ (or aruṣ-/arus-), the gender is not certain. mūrcchā kept as the Sanskrit word.

hindi: (ये) मज्जा के प्रदोष से (होते हैं)। शुक्र के दोष से नपुंसकता और उत्तेजना का अभाव (होते हैं), अथवा (सन्तान) रोगी, नपुंसक, अल्पायु या विरूप उत्पन्न होती है।
english: (These arise) from vitiation of marrow (majjan). From a defect of semen (śukra) come impotence (klaibya) and lack of arousal, or (the offspring) is born diseased, impotent, short-lived or deformed.
notes: SENTENCE: majjapradoṣāt closes the list of 17. The neuter forms rogi, klībam, alpāyuḥ, virūpam agree with an understood neuter noun such as apatya 'offspring'; the noun is not in the text. aharṣaṇa 'lack of arousal' (sexual excitement) is the literal sense.

hindi: और उसका गर्भ उत्पन्न नहीं होता, (या) गिर जाता है, बह भी जाता है; क्योंकि दूषित शुक्र मनुष्य को सन्तान और पत्नी सहित पीड़ित करता है।
english: And no embryo of his is produced; (or) it falls, or it also flows out; for vitiated semen afflicts the man together with his offspring and his wife.
notes: asya 'of him' refers to the man with vitiated semen (from 18). patati 'falls' and prasravati 'flows out' are kept literal (loss of the embryo); the difference between them is not stated.

hindi: जब मल इन्द्रियों का आश्रय लेकर कुपित होते हैं, तब वे इन्द्रियों को उपघात और उपताप से युक्त कर देते हैं।
english: When the malas, lodging in the sense organs, become aggravated, they afflict the sense organs with impairment (upaghāta) and distress (upatāpa).
notes: malāḥ here, aggravated in the organs, are probably the doṣas; kept as 'malas' (मल). yojayanti is literally 'join (them) with'. upaghāta 'impairment, damage' and upatāpa 'distress, burning' kept with literal glosses.

hindi: स्नायु में तथा सिराओं और कण्डराओं से दूषित (मल) मनुष्य को स्तम्भ, संकोच, खल्ली, ग्रन्थि, स्फुरण और सुप्ति से कष्ट देते हैं।
english: (The malas) vitiated in the sinew (snāyu), and from the vessels (sirā) and tendons (kaṇḍarā), torment a man with stiffness, contraction, khallī, granthi (swelling), throbbing and numbness.
notes: The subject (malāḥ) is understood from 20. The cases are mixed as printed: snāyau loc. sg. beside sirākaṇḍarābhyaḥ abl. (or dat.) pl.; the sense 'vitiated in the sinews, vessels and tendons' is clear, but the printed grammar is kept and translated literally. The dvandvas end in the feminine of the last member (khallī, supti). khallī kept in Sanskrit, no identification.

hindi: कुपित दोष मलों का आश्रय लेकर मलों का भेदन, शोषण और प्रदूषण, तथा उनका अत्यधिक रुकना और निकलना उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: The doṣas, aggravated and lodging in the wastes (mala), cause breaking, drying and vitiation of the wastes, and their excessive retention and release.
notes: Here the doṣas and the malas are named separately, so malāḥ = the body's wastes (mala). atīva may qualify only utsarga 'excessive release' or both members; taken with both.

hindi: विविध अहितकर खाए, पिए, चाटे और चबाए गए (आहार) से मनुष्यों के ये विकार होते हैं, जो बताए गए हैं।
english: From various unwholesome (food) eaten, drunk, licked and chewed arise these disorders of men which have been described.
notes: The four ways of taking food (eaten, drunk, licked, chewed) are the chapter's subject (vividha-aśita-pīta); 'food' is understood. ya before u = ye with the vowel elided (e + u > a u).

hindi: उनकी अनुत्पत्ति चाहने वाला बुद्धिमान् सदा हितकर ही अशित आदि (आहार) का सेवन करे; इस प्रकार उनसे उत्पन्न रोग नहीं होंगे।
english: Wishing their non-arising, the intelligent one should always use only wholesome (food) eaten and the rest; so diseases born of that would not arise.
notes: tajjāḥ 'born of that' = born of unwholesome eating etc. (23). tathā 'so' joins the result to the advice ('so that ... would not be').

hindi: रसज विकारों की औषध सब (प्रकार का) लङ्घन है; रक्तज (विकारों) की चिकित्सा विधिशोणितिक अध्याय में (कही गई है)।
english: For disorders born of rasa, all (kinds of) lightening (laṅghana) is the medicine; the treatment of those born of blood (is given) in the Vidhiśoṇitika chapter.
notes: rasa here = the first dhātu (body fluid), not taste. sarvam may also go with auṣadham ('the whole medicine is lightening'). Vidhiśoṇitika is the name of an earlier chapter as printed here (derived name, not split). bhiṣagjita, literally 'what is won by the physician', = treatment.

words.gloss: the action of knife, alkali and fire
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: मांसज (विकारों) की (औषध) संशुद्धि तथा शस्त्र, क्षार और अग्नि कर्म है; मेदोज (विकारों) की चिकित्सा अष्टौनिन्दितिक अध्याय में (कही गई है)।
english: For those born of flesh (māṃsa), (the medicine is) purification and the action of knife, alkali (kṣāra) and fire; the treatment of those born of fat (medas) (is given) in the Aṣṭauninditika chapter.
notes: Aṣṭauninditika is the name of an earlier chapter as printed here (derived name, not split). 'medicine' is understood from 25. tu marks the next item ('and'/'but').

words.gram: n. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. upa-√dhā

hindi: अस्थि में आश्रित व्याधियों की औषध पञ्चकर्म, बस्तियाँ, और तिक्त (द्रव्यों) से युक्त दूध और घी हैं।
english: For diseases residing in bone, the medicine is the five procedures (pañcakarma), enemas (basti), and milk and ghee combined with bitter (drugs).
notes: kṣīrasarpīṃṣi may also mean ghee preparations made with milk ('milk-ghees'); kept as 'milk and ghee'. tiktakopahitāni qualifies the milk and ghee.

words.gloss: of those arising from marrow and semen
words.gram: m. gen. pl., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first members)

hindi: मज्जा और शुक्र से उत्पन्न (विकारों) की औषध मधुर और तिक्त अन्न, व्यवाय और व्यायाम, तथा (उचित) काल में और मात्रा से शुद्धि है।
english: For those arising from marrow and semen, the medicine is sweet and bitter food, sexual intercourse (vyavāya) and exercise, and purification at the (proper) time and in measure (mātrā).
notes: kāle ca mātrayā may apply to all the items, not only to śuddhi 'purification'. svādu here = sweet (the taste).

words.gloss: of those born in the sense organs
of those born of the sinews etc.

hindi: इन्द्रियज (विकारों) की शान्ति तो त्रिमर्मीय में कही जाएगी; स्नायु आदि से उत्पन्न (विकारों) का प्रशमन वातरोगिक में कहा जाएगा।
english: The calming of those born in the sense organs, however, will be told in the Trimarmīya; the alleviation of those born of the sinews (snāyu) and the rest will be told in the Vātarogika.
notes: Trimarmīya and Vātarogika are names of later chapters as printed (derived names, not split); 'chapter' is understood. The future middle forms are used in a passive sense.

hindi: नवेगान्धारण अध्याय में चिकित्सा का संग्रह किया गया है, और मलज विकारों की सिद्धि जहाँ-तहाँ कही गई है।
english: In the Navegāndhāraṇa chapter a summary of treatment has been made, and success (siddhi) over disorders born of the wastes (mala) has been stated here and there.
notes: Navegāndhāraṇa is a chapter name as printed (literally 'not suppressing the urges'), kept whole. It is not explicit whether the summary in that chapter is for the mala disorders only or in general; read with malajānām as the following sentence. mala here = wastes (as in 22).

hindi: व्यायाम से, ऊष्मा की तीक्ष्णता से, हित का आचरण न करने से और मारुत की द्रुतता से मल कोष्ठ से शाखाओं में जाते हैं।
english: From exercise, from the sharpness of heat (ūṣman), from not practising the wholesome, and from the quickness of Vāta (māruta), the malas go from the trunk (koṣṭha) to the periphery (śākhā).
notes: ūṣmaṇaḥ may also be abl. sg. ('from heat, from sharpness'); taken as gen. with taikṣṇyāt. malāḥ moving between trunk and periphery are probably the doṣas (as 47 says doṣāḥ); kept as 'malas'.

words.gloss: at an improper place and time

hindi: और वहाँ स्थित (मल), कभी प्रेरित न होने पर, ठहरे रहते हैं; कारण की प्रतीक्षा करते हुए वे अनुचित देश-काल में फिर कुपित नहीं होते।
english: And staying there they linger, at times not being set in motion; waiting for a cause, they do not become aggravated again at an improper place and time.
notes: bhūyaḥ may also go with hetu ('waiting for a further cause'). kadācin na samīritāḥ is read 'when sometimes not stirred'.

words.gloss: from cleansing of the mouths of the channels

hindi: वृद्धि से, विष्यन्द से, पाक से, स्रोतों के मुखों के विशोधन से और वायु के निग्रह से मल शाखाओं को छोड़कर कोष्ठ में जाते हैं।
english: Through increase, liquefaction (viṣyanda), ripening (pāka), cleansing of the mouths of the channels (srotas), and the restraint of Vāta (vāyu), the malas leave the periphery and go to the trunk.

text_flags.why: possible: there is no noun viṣyandāna; the action noun of vi-√syand is viṣyandana; with light da the syllables 5-7 run ⏑ – – (regular pathyā); the count (8) is the same
possible: there is no word viśothana; viśodhana 'cleansing' (vi-√śudh) differs only by th/dh and gives the sense 'cleansing of the mouths of the channels'

notes: The words are split from the conjectured viṣyandanāt and srotomukhaviśodhanāt (see text_flags). yanti is a regular form of √i 'go' (beside yānti in 31), not a typo. pāka here = ripening (of the malas), not inflammation. malāḥ = probably the doṣas, as in 31.

words.gram: m. gen. pl., ppp. √jan with a-

hindi: रोगों में से जो उत्पन्न नहीं हुए उनकी अनुत्पत्ति के लिए और जो उत्पन्न हो गए उनकी निवृत्ति के लिए जो विधि देखी गई है, सुख चाहने वाला उसका आचरण करे।
english: The method that has been seen for the non-arising of diseases not yet arisen and for the removal of those that have arisen, one who seeks happiness should practise it.
notes: rogāṇām goes with both ajātānām and jātānām.

words.gloss: from the difference of knowledge and ignorance
words.gram: m. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

words.gloss: activities on the right path and the wrong path
words.gram: f. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: सब प्राणियों की सब प्रवृत्तियाँ सुख के लिए मानी गई हैं; किन्तु ज्ञान और अज्ञान के भेद से मार्ग और अमार्ग में प्रवृत्तियाँ (होती हैं)।
english: All the activities of all beings are held to be for the sake of happiness; but from the difference (viśeṣa) of knowledge and ignorance (come) activities on the right path and on the wrong path.

text_flags.why: possible: the word must agree with f. nom. pl. matāḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ; before s- followed by a vowel the visarga is kept (or becomes s), not dropped

notes: The split uses the conjectured sukhārthāḥ (see text_flag). mārga/amārga literally 'path/non-path'.

words.gloss: whose selves are covered by rajas and delusion
words.gram: m. nom. pl., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: परीक्षक भली-भाँति परीक्षा करके हित का ही अनुसरण करते हैं; किन्तु रज और मोह से आवृत आत्मा वाले लौकिक लोग प्रिय का ही (अनुसरण करते हैं)।
english: The examiners, having examined carefully, pursue only the wholesome; but worldly people, whose selves are covered by rajas and delusion, (pursue) only the pleasant.
notes: parīkṣaka 'examiner' = the one who examines before acting. rajas kept Sanskrit.

hindi: श्रुत, बुद्धि, स्मृति, दाक्ष्य, धृति, हित का सेवन, वाणी की विशुद्धि, शम और धैर्य परीक्षक का आश्रय लेते हैं।
english: Learning, intellect, memory, dexterity, steadfastness, the use of the wholesome, purity of speech, calm and fortitude resort to the examiner.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members), ppp. √śri

hindi: मोह और रज के आश्रित लौकिक (व्यक्ति) का ये गुण आश्रय नहीं लेते; उस मूल वाले अनेक शारीरिक और मानसिक रोग आते हैं।
english: These qualities do not resort to the worldly person, who is attached to delusion and rajas; rooted in that, many diseases, bodily and mental, come about.
notes: tanmūlāḥ 'having that as root': 'that' is the worldly person's state (attachment to delusion and rajas, without these qualities). yanti 'go, come' is kept literal.

hindi: क्योंकि प्रज्ञापराध से (मनुष्य) पाँच अहितकर (इन्द्रिय-)अर्थों का सेवन करता है, वेगों को रोकता है और साहस के कार्यों का सेवन करता है।
english: For through the offence of intellect (prajñāparādha) one uses the five unwholesome objects (of the senses), suppresses the urges (vega), and engages in rash acts.
notes: arthān pañca = the five objects of the senses ('of the senses' understood).

words.gram: n. loc. sg., ppp. √kṛ with amalī (cvi)

hindi: अज्ञ तात्कालिक सुख कहलाने वाले भावों में अनुरक्त होता है; किन्तु ज्ञाता अनुरक्त नहीं होता, क्योंकि विज्ञान निर्मल कर दिया गया होता है।
english: The ignorant one becomes attached to things called pleasant for the moment; but the knower is not attached, for his knowledge (vijñāna) has been made stainless.
notes: vijñāne amalīkṛte is a locative absolute ('knowledge having been made stainless'); 'his' is supplied in the English.

hindi: न राग से और न ही अविज्ञान से आहारों का उपयोग करे; परीक्षा करके हितकर (आहार) खाए, क्योंकि देह आहार से उत्पन्न होती है।
english: One should not use foods out of attachment (rāga), nor out of lack of knowledge; one should eat the wholesome after examining it, for the body arises from food.

text_flags.why: metre: 'na arāgān...' gives 17 syllables in the half-line, 'na rāgān...' gives 16; 'na a-' is also left in hiatus without sandhi; rāga 'attachment' pairs with avijñāna and with anurajyate/rajyate in 40

notes: The words follow the conjectured 'na rāgān' (see text_flag); as printed, 'arāgāt' would mean 'from non-attachment', which does not fit the sense.

words.gloss: in the arising of good and bad
words.gram: f. loc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: आहार की विधि में शुभ और अशुभ की उत्पत्ति में हेतु कहलाने वाले आठ विशेष हैं; उनकी परीक्षा करके (आहार का) प्रयोग करे।
english: In the method of food there are eight particulars (viśeṣa) known as causes in the arising of good and bad; having examined them, one should apply (food).

text_flags.why: metre: the half-line has 7 syllables in its first quarter with āḥrasya and 8 with āhārasya; there is no word āḥra; āhāra is the subject of 41 and 45 in this chunk
no word sājñaka; saṃjñaka 'called' (cf. -saṃjñeṣu in 40 of this chunk); syllable count unchanged
the space is misplaced: 'aprayojayet' is not a form (the augment a- is not used with the optative); read parīkṣya (abs.) + prayojayet (opt.), as parīkṣya in 41

notes: The split follows the three corrections in text_flags. The eight particulars are not listed in this verse. prayojayet has no object in the line; '(food)' is supplied.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. pari-√hṛ

hindi: त्याग करने योग्य अपथ्यों का सदा परिहार करता हुआ पण्डित मनुष्य यहाँ साधुओं की अनृणता को प्राप्त हो जाता है।
english: A wise man who always avoids the unwholesome things that are to be avoided becomes here one who has attained the freedom from debt (anṛṇatā) of the good.
notes: sādhūnām may mean 'towards the good' (freedom from debt to them) or 'of the good' (the debt-free state that the good have); kept literal. paṇḍitaḥ may also be the predicate ('becomes wise').

hindi: किन्तु रोग का जो कारण यहाँ किसी के द्वारा टाला नहीं जा सकता, उसके प्राप्त होने पर मनीषियों को शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
english: But the cause of disease which here cannot be avoided by anyone: on meeting with it, the wise should not grieve.
notes: śocitavyam is impersonal ('it should not be grieved by the wise').

words.gloss: from the difference of wholesome and unwholesome
words.gram: m. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं: आहार से उत्पन्न वस्तु और आहार से उत्पन्न रोग; और हित तथा अहित के भेद से सुख और दुःख का भेद;
english: Here, the verses: the entity arising from food, and diseases arising from food; and the difference of happiness and misery from the difference of wholesome and unwholesome;

text_flags.why: agreement: the word qualifies n. vastu; also -aḥ before v- would appear as -o, so the printed visarga is not a sandhi form

notes: Summary verses of the chapter (45-48), a list of topics. vastu 'the entity' is probably the body (cf. 41 deho hy āhārasaṃbhavaḥ); kept literal. The split uses the conjectured āhārasaṃbhavaṃ (see text_flag).

hindi: दुःखों को सहने और न सहने में देह और सत्त्व का भेद; और धातुओं से उत्पन्न जो रोग-समूह अलग-अलग (हैं);
english: the difference between body and mind (sattva) in bearing and not bearing sufferings; and the groups of diseases which arise from the dhātus, each separately;

text_flags.why: the printed form has both m and ṃ; one of them is a typing slip (gen. pl. duḥkhānām)
doubled c is a typing slip: ś + ca (sandhi of -āḥ ca), as in rogāścāhāra- in 45

notes: deha-sattvayoḥ 'of body and mind': sattva = mind (sattva).

hindi: और उनका प्रशमन भी; दोष कोष्ठ से शाखाओं में जाकर और शाखाओं से कोष्ठ में आकर जिस प्रकार कुपित होते हैं;
english: and also their alleviation; how the doṣas become aggravated having gone from the trunk to the periphery, and having come from the periphery to the trunk;

words.gloss: of the wise and the ignorant
wholesome for the healthy and the patient
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)
n. nom. sg., ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś

hindi: और प्राज्ञ तथा अज्ञ का भेद, और जो स्वस्थ और आतुर के लिए हितकर है — वह सब विविधाशितपीतीय में भली-भाँति प्रकाशित किया गया है।
english: and the difference between the wise and the ignorant, and what is wholesome for the healthy and the patient: all that has been fully explained in the Vividhāśitapītīya.
notes: Vividhāśitapītīya is the name of this chapter (derived name, not split).

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के सूत्रस्थान में विविधाशितपीतीय नामक अट्ठाईसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Sūtra section (Sūtrasthāna), the twenty-eighth chapter named Vividhāśitapītīya.
notes: Chapter colophon (prose).
